task.description: WF-03 step 3 for ISS-0002 (HIGH): implement the fix exactly as design v4 §4.1, §5.1-§5.7, §6 (E_WRITE) and §7 describe and decisions/0004 records: no in-place writes; new bytes go to a temp file next to each target (exclusive create, flushed to disk, target's mode), the old file is kept as a hard link, renames in order with STATE.md last, rollback from the hard links if a rename fails, cleanup at the end; prepare-run builds the whole run folder under a temporary name and commits it with one rename; any handled failure gives exit 1, only E_WRITE lines (catalogue in §5.6), no stack trace and a strict listing of <root> unchanged; leftovers of an interrupted run are refused by name and never deleted by the command; only OS errors become E_WRITE, a program bug still crashes with its trace (no catch-all); symlinked targets and symlinked folders on the way to a target are refused; the failure-injection tests patch node:fs, so call fs through its namespace (as the design §9.2 requires) so that patches reach your code. result.summary:
BACKEND-DEV, WF-03 step 4 for ISS-0002. Implemented design v4 (docs/design/REQ-002-idea-verdict.md, sha256 fd2b8f81...) sections 4.1, 5.1-5.7, 6 (E_WRITE) and 7 in the three files of the write set. cli.js, validate.js, snapshot.js, tools/test/, package.json and eslint.config.js are untouched: the manifest of tools/ (sha256 per file, node_modules excluded) differs before/after in exactly apply.js, prepare.js and util.js. Next: REVIEWER.

SAFETY. apply-verdict and prepare-run were never run against the real root, runs/ or STATE.md. Every run used temp projects (os.tmpdir() fixtures of tools/test/helpers.js, or my scratch TMPDIR) or scratch copies of sai/; my scratch runner refuses any --root outside the scratch folder. Real files, before -> after my work: STATE.md sha256 e5ef7412f59c8b8ad0b4d50b0f1edbb8ba6796e7a8d5de1592605d5786945c19 -> the same (15639 B, mode 0644, mtime 1790787984 also the same). runs/ content manifest (sha256 of every file, sorted) 71d9a79e705e219be2d303b044713ee6ae6dd75f3acabb950b58c94a220dc594 -> the same; runs/ stat manifest (type, mode, size, mtime of every entry, folders included) 4eae08336076d1dd9f98b3d7510952e07406df362163b31df9726f0061802a00 -> the same. No .sai-* entry anywhere in the real project.

CHECKS (real output, cd tools). npm run check -> exit 0: prettier 'All matched files use Prettier code style!'; eslint . --max-warnings 0 prints nothing; node --test: tests 115, suites 0, pass 115, fail 0, cancelled 0, skipped 0, todo 0. The same three commands run separately (format:check, lint, test): exit 0, exit 0, 115/115. Baseline before my change: also 115/115, format and lint clean. No eslint-disable, no skip, nothing masked (Q6).

EXISTING TESTS THAT FAIL: none. No existing test exercises a behaviour that design 5.4 changes (read-only folder, symbolic links), so none had to change. One design-predicted test-side effect, not a defect of the code: with the strict tree() of design 9.2 swapped into a scratch copy of helpers.js, the 51 tests of the 7 files that use tree() or chmod (apply.accept, apply.escalate, apply.reject, apply.state, cli, prepare, validate.run) pass 51/51 under umask 022; under umask 077 exactly one fails, cli.test.js 'validate: unreadable verdict-1.md ...' (the literal 0o644 restore, design 9.2, F3). That is TEST-DESIGNER's edit.

BEHAVIOURS B1-B30 (design 9.1) -> CODE. All functions are in tools/src/util.js unless stated. 'scratch rows' = my own harness rows named like the design's test rows (see VERIFICATION).
B1 no in-place write, no truncated target -> stage() writes only .<name>.sai-tmp (fs.writeFileSync flag wx, flush true) and commit() renames; the target path is never opened for writing (scratch W30-W35, W48).
B2 target is a folder -> inspect() W1.2 lstat isDirectory: 'is a folder (EISDIR)' (W06-W09, W23).
B3 target is a symbolic link, also dangling -> inspect() W1.2 lstat isSymbolicLink: 'is a symbolic link (ELOOP)' (W10-W12).
B4 a folder on the way is a link -> inspect() W1.1: lstat of each folder between root and target, outermost first, so both runs/<RUN-ID> (W13) and runs (W13b) are caught; prepare-run: createFolderAllOrNothing() P1 (P04).
B5 leftover .sai-tmp/.sai-old refused, also when nothing must change -> inspect() W1.3 (before the read, so also for unchanged targets); stage() maps EEXIST of wx/link to the same 'leftover' line (race); createFolderAllOrNothing() P1 and EEXIST of the non-recursive mkdir (W14, W15, W47, W48; P06, P13, P14).
B6 target unreadable for comparison -> inspect() W1.4 'cannot be read for comparison'; STATE.md unreadable stays E_STATE_ANCHOR before the write phase (apply.js, unchanged) (W16, W17, W18).
B7 read-only target: refuse only if it must change -> inspect() W1.5 (equal bytes: plan.changes=false, W1.6 skipped) then W1.6 fs.accessSync W_OK (W19-W22).
B8 read-only folder: refuse only if something there must change -> consequence of stage(): only changing targets get a temp file; 'cannot write the temporary file ... (EACCES)' (W24-W29).
B9 preparation failure leaves nothing -> stage() + undo(): everything in journal.created is unlinked in reverse creation order (W24-W26, W28-W34, W36, W37).
B10 exclusive create: a foreign temp file is neither overwritten nor deleted -> stage(): wx; on EEXIST the entry is forgotten so undo() never removes it; refused() builds the leftover line (W38).
B11 failed rename k -> roll back 1..k-1 -> commit() throws, writeAllOrNothing() catch calls undo(): rename .sai-old back over the target (existing target) or unlink (created target), newest first (W39-W43).
B12 STATE.md replaced last -> apply.js passes targets [proposed-actions.json, apply-report.json, STATE.md] (escalate: [apply-report.json, STATE.md]); writeAllOrNothing() commits in the given order (W41-W43, W47).
B13 interruption: each target old or new, next run refuses, converges after deleting leftovers -> stage() makes every temp file and hard link before the first rename, rename is atomic; prepare-run builds under a temp name and commits with one rename; the refusal is B5 (W47, W48; P13, P14).
B14 failed cleanup after a failure -> extra line, targets unchanged -> undo() collects 'could not remove this temporary file/backup of the old version' lines, outcome 'no target was changed; leftovers are listed next'; prepare-run: P4 rmSync failure line 'could not remove this temporary folder' (W44; P11).
B15 failed rollback -> lines say what remains -> undo(): 'rollback failed (code); it holds the new content, the old content is in <.sai-old>' or '... it was created by this run and is still there'; the backup is kept; outcome 'rollback incomplete; see the next lines' (W45).
B16 failed cleanup after the commit -> code 1 -> writeAllOrNothing() W4 loop: 'applied, but this backup of the old version could not be removed (code); delete it by hand'; the count of replaced targets is still returned, cli.js prints the line and returns 1 (W46).
B17 all violations at once, in target order -> writeAllOrNothing() runs inspect() on every target (each stops at its first violation) and prints all before returning 0 (W13, W23).
B18 unchanged targets are not touched -> inspect() W1.5; writeAllOrNothing() filters plan.changes; all unchanged returns 0, cli.js prints 'unchanged' (W04, W22, W27; second apply).
B19 permissions of a replaced target kept, new targets default -> inspect() keeps stat.mode & 0o777; stage() fs.chmodSync(tmp) before the link; a new target keeps the default mode of writeFileSync (W05, W01; extra probe umask 077).
B20 program error is not E_WRITE, rollback done -> isOsError() (string code AND syscall); osCall()/refused() pass any other exception through; writeAllOrNothing() and createFolderAllOrNothing() undo/clean first, then rethrow it unchanged (W49).
B21 E_WRITE: code 1, empty stdout, exact lines, no trace -> addFailure() builds 'E_WRITE <file>: <reason> (<code>); <outcome>[; if no other command is running, delete and re-run]' into the caller's Issues; cli.js unchanged (checks A1-A4 on every row).
B22 after the cause is removed it converges to the clean bytes -> no state is kept between runs; targets are compared by bytes (A6 on every row).
B23 escalate never creates proposed-actions.json -> apply.js: proposed is undefined in escalate mode (W03, W09, W25, W33, W43).
B24 prepare-run: the folder appears with one rename, nothing created on failure -> createFolderAllOrNothing() P2 (temp folder, files with wx+flush), P3 one fs.renameSync, P4 fs.rmSync of the temp folder (P05, P07-P11).
B25 prepare-run: runs is a file or a link -> createFolderAllOrNothing() P1: 'is not a folder (ENOTDIR)', 'is a symbolic link (ELOOP)' (P03, P04).
B26 prepare-run: runs missing -> created together with the run folder -> P1 takes the first missing folder as the top, so the temp folder is .runs.sai-tmp and the run folder is built inside it under <RUN-ID>/ (P02, P08).
B27 prepare-run: anything at the run folder path, even a dangling link -> E_USAGE code 2 -> prepare.js occupied(): lstat instead of existsSync; any OS error of lstat means 'no entry' and is left to P1 (P12 plus the existing 'E_USAGE: bad RUN-ID and existing folder').
B28 strict listing sees folders, modes, links, times, ignores folder time -> test code only (tree() in tools/test/helpers.js); nothing in my write set; used by my scratch harness with the 9.2 definition.
B29 an lstat error is a violation, not 'no target' -> entryAt(): ENOENT is 'no entry', any other OS error is 'cannot be checked (code)'; prepare.js occupied() does not throw on it (W50; P03).
B30 target is a pipe or socket -> 'is not a regular file (EINVAL)', judged in inspect() W1.2 before the read in W1.4, so a pipe cannot hang the command (W51, W52).

VERIFICATION BEYOND THE SUITE (scratch, outside the repo: <вне проекта>/bd-iss0002/harness/, run: node run-all.mjs). I implemented the fault-injection contract of design 9.2 (SAI_TEST_FAULTS, --import), the strict tree(), and all 67 rows W01-W52, W13b, P01-P14 through the real CLI in child processes with real SIGKILL, a real mkfifo pipe, a real socket, real ulimit -f 1 (EFBIG), chmod 000/444/555. Fixed code: 67 of 67 pass, also with the temp root behind a symbolic link (lexical paths). Pre-fix code (pristine copies of the three files in a scratch tools/): 10 pass (W01-W05, W18, W22, W27, P01, P02: the design's 'fixation' rows) and 57 fail, as the design's 'before the fix' column predicts. Mutants of design 9.7 applied to scratch copies of my code and caught by the rows the design names: M1 (W47, W48), M2 (W40-W43), M3 (W28-W34, W36, W37), M4 (W15, W47, W48), M5 (W19-W21), M6 (W10-W12), M7 (W13, W13b, P04), M8 (W49), M9 (W05, W36), M10 (W04, W22, W27), M11 (W38), M12 (W38), M14 (P07-P10, P11), M15 (W01-W05, W46), M17 (W50), M19 (W13b only). Extra probes, all pass: file with the Finder lock flag (chflags uchg) -> 'is read-only and must change (EPERM)'; STATE.md with a second hard link; umask 077; the replaced STATE.md is a new inode and the old inode still holds the old bytes; 100 simultaneous pairs of apply-verdict on one project: never a stack trace, never a half state, one side applies or refuses with E_WRITE leftover lines, and after deleting the named leftovers it converges to the clean bytes; validate ignores .sai- leftovers (exit 0) and snapshot lists leftover files but not an empty temp folder (design 5.5). End to end on scratch copies of the whole real sai/ (no node_modules, no .git): validate OK; apply-verdict on the real run WF06-20260926-01 gives 'applied recommend' then 'unchanged' with the old and the new code, and the two copies are byte-identical afterwards (diff -r empty outside tools/src); prepare-run of a new run id on both copies prints the same seal and creates a byte-identical runs/; validate --stage run --seal accepts it. A message-text check: every E_WRITE phrase of design 5.6 appears verbatim in util.js, and none is invented.

NOT VERIFIED: a filesystem without hard links (only simulated by an injected EPERM on link, W37); power loss (not promised, design 5.2); Linux; running as root (the design assumes non-root); the FAT case of 5.4.

OPEN QUESTIONS for ORCH/REVIEWER.
1. util.js has a third new export, isOsError(). Design 5.7 lists two new exports and calls the OS-error test internal. prepare.js needs it so that its lstat check swallows only OS errors (a bare catch would be a catch-all, Q6). Alternative if you want exactly two exports: a bare catch there, like readTextFile has.
2. Design 5.6 does not say which path goes in <file> in two cases; I chose: for 'cannot be checked' the path whose lstat failed (the target, a folder on the way, or a leftover name); for prepare-run lines about the temporary folder, the rename and 'leftover', the topmost missing folder: <R> when runs/ exists (as P05, P06, P10 show) and runs when it does not (no row covers that case).
3. Program-error path: undo() runs, then the exception goes on unchanged (design 5.3), so if the rollback or cleanup also fails at that moment no E_WRITE line says so (nobody prints Issues when an exception propagates). No row covers it; I left it as the design words it. A design edit would be needed to change it.
4. For ORCH, pre-existing and unrelated to this change: the real apply-report.json of WF06-20260926-01 records an older STATE.md sha256 than the current STATE.md, so the next real apply-verdict on that run will answer 'applied recommend' and rewrite only apply-report.json (seen on the scratch copy; old and new code give identical bytes). It will now be safe to run (all or nothing), but it is a data change.
5. The existing tests need the design's test-side edits (strict tree(), the 0o644 literal) by TEST-DESIGNER; see EXISTING TESTS above.
No quality-bar item was lowered or needed an exception: Q3 (no 'works' without a real run; every claim above has its run), Q4 (one check command, real output), Q6, Q10, Q11 (writes stay inside <root>: link targets and links on the way are refused; verified W11, W13, W13b, P04) all hold. Nothing was committed, pushed or written outside the three source files and this handoff.

changes.change: +460 lines, 0 removed (every existing export is byte-identical, listFiles untouched). New section 'Write phase, all or nothing': exports writeAllOrNothing(root, targets, issues) -> number of targets that now hold new content, 0 when nothing changed on disk, E_WRITE lines only, throws only a program error after rollback and cleanup (design 5.3 W1-W4, 5.6, 5.7) and createFolderAllOrNothing(root, rel, files, issues) -> true/false, P1-P4; plus isOsError(err) (string code and syscall). Internals: WriteFailure, Journal (what this run created and which targets were renamed), inspect (W1.1-W1.6), stage (temp file wx+flush, chmod, hard link), commit (rename), undo (rollback newest first, then cleanup in reverse creation order, extra lines in target order), W4 loop. All fs calls go through the default fs object (never destructured), paths are lexical, as design 9.2 requires for fault injection.

+35/-30. The in-place loop (fs.existsSync + fs.readFileSync + fs.writeFileSync, old lines 100-107) is replaced by writeAllOrNothing(root, targets, issues) with targets in commit order proposed-actions.json (recommend only), apply-report.json, STATE.md last. Content of every target is computed as before; 'written' in apply-report.json is still STATE.md, then proposed-actions.json. 'import fs' removed (unused), writeAllOrNothing imported, the comment on the check phase extended to the write phase. Return shape { issues, mode, changed } unchanged.

+28/-7. fs.existsSync(runDir) -> occupied(): fs.lstatSync, so any entry at the run folder path, a dangling link included, is E_USAGE (code 2); an OS error of lstat means 'no entry' (design 4.1), a program error is rethrown. The write (mkdir recursive + writeFileSync per copy, then run.json) -> createFolderAllOrNothing(root, runs/<RUN-ID>, files, issues) with the copies in run.sources order and run.json last; false returns { issues }. Imports createFolderAllOrNothing and isOsError added. Validation order, messages and the returned { issues, runDir, seal } are unchanged.
